name: Heritability Coefficient Calculator
seoDesc: Heritability is the share of the variation in a trait, in one population in one environment, that is attributable to genetic differences. Free heritability co
summary:
Heritability is the share of the variation in a trait, in one population in one environment, that is attributable to genetic differences. It returns heritability from parent-offspring regression, heritability from half-sib correlation, heritability from variance components and response to selection, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator estimates narrow-sense heritability from parent-offspring or half-sib data and shows the expected response to selection. The arithmetic keeps full precision internally and only rounds what it displays, so the number you copy out is the number the formula produced. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Heritability Coefficient
sections.html:
h² = V_A ÷ (V_A + V_E); h² = 2r(parent, offspring); h² = 4r(half sibs); R = h² × S

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
V_Aadditive genetic variance—
V_Eenvironmental variance—
Sselection differentialSD
Rresponse to selectionSD

sections.title: How do I use the Heritability Coefficient?
sections.html:
Fill the boxes you have numbers for; the calculator decides what it can derive from them.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: correlation between parent and offspring of 0.35, correlation among half sibs of 0.09, additive genetic variance of 0.4, environmental variance of 0.6, selection differential of 1.2 SD.

Substituting them into the formula gives heritability from parent-offspring regression of 0.7, heritability from half-sib correlation of 0.36, heritability from variance components of 0.4, response to selection of 0.48 SD.

Because the example uses the defaults, you can reproduce it by loading the page and reading the results panel before touching anything.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
Interpretation is a convention, not part of the arithmetic. The usual bands are:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
0 – 0.2Lowenvironment dominates; breeding progress is slow
0.2 – 0.4Moderatetypical for growth and yield traits
0.4 – 0.7Hightypical for body size and milk yield
0.7 – 1.0Very highhighly canalised traits such as coat pattern

  • Heritability is a property of a population in an environment, not of a gene. The same trait can be 0.6 in a uniform greenhouse and 0.2 in a variable field.

  • Narrow-sense heritability counts only additive effects, because that is the part that responds to selection; broad-sense includes dominance and interaction.

  • The breeder's equation R = h²S is the most useful form: it turns heritability into a prediction of how much the next generation moves.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
Before blaming the formula, check these — they explain nearly every mismatch:

  • Quoting a heritability figure for a trait without saying which population and environment.
  • Using a parent-offspring correlation from different environments, which inflates h².
  • Assuming that a high heritability means a trait cannot be changed by the environment.

faq.q: What is the difference between h² and H²?
faq.a: h² (narrow sense) is additive variance over total; H² (broad sense) is all genetic variance over total. Only h² predicts selection response.
Not in a properly estimated design; a value above 1 signals a data or model error.

faq.q: What does the Heritability Coefficient actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns heritability from parent-offspring regression, heritability from half-sib correlation, heritability from variance components and response to selection. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
